story.head: The Devils’ power play outclasses the Blues’
paras: The Devils won the teams’ first meeting this season, 5-4 in overtime in New Jersey on Nov 5. The Blues have won two in a row, while the Devils (15-7-0) lost 3-2 to Montréal on Wednesday. Going in, the Devils are second in the Metropolitan (tied for eighth in the NHL) and the Blues seventh in the Central (18th).

The Blues (lowest) and the Devils (3rd lowest) both keep things calm after the whistle. The Devils rarely throw hits (2nd lowest) and draw more penalties than they take (3rd). The Blues ice the puck less than anyone (1st) and take a lot of high-quality shots (3rd). The Devils’ power play bites, but the Blues’ doesn’t.

Jack Hughes (10 G / 17 A / 27 P in 22 GP) leads the Devils in scoring, and Jesper Bratt (4 G / 18 A / 22 P in 22 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Blues, Robert Thomas (4 G / 16 A / 20 P in 22 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eight points in his last five games and four goals in six games against New Jersey since 2023-24. Jimmy Snuggerud (12 G / 5 A / 17 P in 22 GP) has a team-high twelve goals.
Connor Hellebuyck (7-1-0 / .913 SV% in 8 GS) has been terrific for New Jersey and will likely start. Joel Hofer (9-6-1 / .923 SV% in 16 GS) has been outstanding for St. Louis and will likely start.
At home, Jim Montgomery likes to send Dvorský, Suter and Toropchenko out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Boqvist, Glass and Hämeenaho.
